topic: Lambda Design for Deferred Evaluation versus Nested `std::bind`
explanation: When using `std::bind`, the only mechanism available to force deferred evaluation of an argument expression is to wrap that expression in another callable object, typically a nested call to `std::bind`. This instructs the outer `std::bind` to store the inner bind object, which is then invoked when the outer object is called. This nesting significantly increases syntactic complexity and reduces readability, especially when compared to a lambda, where using the expression directly in the body achieves deferred evaluation naturally and clearly.
practical_example: A team maintains legacy code using `std::bind` for complex partial function application. They find that every time an argument needs to be calculated dynamically at call time (instead of bind time), they must introduce a layer of nesting, leading to deeply indented and difficult-to-debug binding chains.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
